readerTitle: Why Toyota lets any worker stop the factory
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Toyota, GM·Toyota 합작 NUMMI) + 가상 적용 (급여 대행 회사)
insight: 문제가 생긴 그 자리에서 멈추고 원인까지 고치면, 멈춤은 손실이 아니라 개선의 출발점이 된다.
misconception: 라인을 멈추지 않고 끝에서 검사하고 고치는 편이 생산량과 비용 면에서 더 낫다.

sources.text: Toyota Motor Corporation, 'Toyota Production System' (jidoka, Sakichi Toyoda's automatic loom)
Ohno, T. (1988). Toyota Production System: Beyond Large-Scale Production. Productivity Press.
Shook, J. (2010). How to Change a Culture: Lessons From NUMMI. MIT Sloan Management Review.
Womack, J., Jones, D., Roos, D. (1990). The Machine That Changed the World.

factChecks.note: NUMMI: GM이 1982년 프리몬트 공장을 닫았고, 1984년 GM·Toyota 합작으로 재가동했으며 기존 노동자 상당수가 재고용되었다는 내용을 This American Life 403회와 Shook(2010)으로 확인하세요. 재고용 비율은 수치로 쓰지 않았습니다.
재가동 후 품질이 일본 Toyota 공장 수준에 가까워졌다는 평가는 Womack 외(1990)와 This American Life 403회에 나옵니다. 구체적 결함 수치나 결근율은 일부러 넣지 않았습니다.
안돈 줄의 작동 방식(줄을 당기면 팀 리더가 오고, 정해진 시간 안에 해결되지 않으면 라인이 멈춤)은 Toyota 공식 자료와 Shook(2010)으로 확인하세요.
Sakichi Toyoda의 자동 직기(실이 끊어지면 스스로 멈춤)는 1920년대(G형 자동직기, 1924년)로 Toyota 공식 자료에 나옵니다. 카드에는 'In the 1920s'로만 적었습니다.
GM이 NUMMI 방식을 다른 공장으로 옮기는 데 성과가 고르지 않았다는 내용은 This American Life 403회의 보도에 근거합니다. 카드에는 'widely reported as uneven'으로 일반화해 적었습니다.
급여 대행 회사 사례는 설명용 가상 사례이며 고객 수 40곳은 가정입니다.

cards.title: Why Toyota lets any worker stop the factory
body: On a Toyota assembly line, a worker who spots a problem can pull a cord above their station. A team leader comes at once. If the problem isn't fixed in time, the whole line stops.
At most car plants, stopping the line was the one thing you never did. Toyota built its system around it.

image.label: Worker reaching for a cord above an assembly line
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 자동차 조립 라인 위에 노란 줄이 걸려 있고, 작업자 한 명이 줄을 당기려 손을 뻗는 순간. 라인 위 신호등이 노란색으로 켜짐. 실제 자동차 브랜드 로고나 엠블럼은 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Should the workers get the cord?
body: It's 1984. GM and Toyota are reopening a closed GM plant in Fremont, California, as a joint venture called NUMMI. Many of the old workers are rehired. The plant had a reputation for poor quality.
You're setting up the new line. A worker spots a part that isn't fitted right. What should the system let them do?

options.text: Keep the line moving and fix defects in a repair area at the end
options.feedback: You protect output today. But the defect gets buried under more parts, repair costs more, and the same mistake keeps happening because nobody traces it.

options.text: Let any worker call for help and, if needed, stop the line
options.feedback: You lose some output at first. In return, every problem surfaces where it starts, while the cause is still visible and cheap to fix.

options.text: Let only supervisors decide whether to stop the line
options.feedback: It feels more controlled, but it's slower. By the time a supervisor arrives, more cars may have passed with the same fault.

cards.title: The same workers, a very different plant.
body: NUMMI gave every worker the cord. Pulls were common at first, and team leaders were expected to respond and help, not to blame.
Within a few years, a plant once known as one of GM's worst was reported to build cars with quality close to Toyota's plants in Japan, with many of the same people on the line.
The workers hadn't changed. **The system around them had.**

image.label: Same workers, two plants: before and after
image.brief: 좌우 분할 일러스트. 왼쪽: 라인 끝에 수리 대기 차량이 길게 쌓인 어두운 공장. 오른쪽: 같은 얼굴의 작업자들이 줄을 당기고 팀 리더가 달려오는 밝은 공장. 실제 로고 없음.

cards.title: Build quality in at the source
body: Toyota calls it *jidoka*. To **build quality in at the source** means stopping work the moment something is wrong, fixing it there, then fixing the cause so it doesn't come back.

The idea is older than Toyota's cars. In the 1920s, Sakichi Toyoda, whose company grew into Toyota, built a loom that stopped itself when a thread broke. One person could watch many machines instead of hunting for flawed cloth later.

image.label: A loom that stops itself when a thread breaks
image.brief: 옛날 자동 직기 일러스트. 실 한 가닥이 끊어진 지점에 작은 경고 표시가 뜨고 직기가 멈춤. 옆에 '문제 발생 → 즉시 정지 → 원인 수정' 흐름을 작은 아이콘 3개로 표시. 로고 없음.

cards.title: Every stop starts a short loop.
body: Each pull of the cord sets off the same steps:
list: **Signal:** a team leader comes at once
**Fix:** solve it on the spot, or stop the line
**Find the cause:** keep asking "why?" until you reach the root
**Change the standard:** update how the work is done
cards.callout: A stop isn't a failure. It's the start of an improvement.
cards.softwareNote: Many software teams use the same idea: when an automated test fails, no new code can be merged until someone fixes it. A small stop now beats hunting the bug after release.

cards.title: A cord without a response is just a rope.
body: GM sent managers to learn from NUMMI and tried to bring its methods to other plants. The results were widely reported as uneven.

Hanging a cord is easy. But if a pull led to blame, or nobody came quickly, workers soon stopped pulling. The real system was the habit behind the cord: respond to every problem fast, and treat it as a fact to fix, not a fault to hide.

cards.title: Stopping has real costs.
body: Early on, frequent stops mean lower output. Toyota accepts that because each fix makes later stops rarer. A business that panics after one slow week will give up too soon.

It also needs two conditions. People can only spot "abnormal" if everyone knows what normal looks like. And help must arrive in minutes. In a team inside a larger company, such as finance closing the month, that means someone clearly owns each signal.

cards.title: Now it's a payroll services firm.
body: You run payroll for 40 business clients. Errors keep turning up at the final check before payday: wrong tax codes, missed new hires. Your reviewers catch most of them, but every cycle ends in late nights.

options.text: Hire another reviewer for the final check
options.feedback: Fewer errors reach clients, but you pay more every cycle and the errors keep being made upstream.

options.text: When an error is found, pause that client's run, trace which step caused it, and fix that step
options.feedback: Slower this month. But each fixed step removes a whole type of error, so the final check gets lighter over time.

options.text: Send errors back to the preparer with a note to be more careful
options.feedback: Quick and cheap, but it treats the person as the cause. People start hiding small mistakes, and the step that allows them stays broken.

cards.title: Stop small problems where they start.
body: Toyota's line works because problems surface early, help arrives fast, and every stop changes how the work is done.
**Try it today:** pick one mistake that keeps coming back. Find where it's first made, not where it's caught, and ask "why?" until you reach a cause you can fix.
